thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Gains 120 Points, But Tech And Internet-relate Stocks Sink Nasdaq

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Gains 120 Points, But Tech And Internet-relate Stocks Sink Nasdaq
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
Iranian oil-export sanctions take effect
U.S. stocks were mixed during midday trade Monday, ahead of an updated policy statement from the Federal Reserve and midterm elections that could alter the balance of power in Washington.
How did benchmarks fare?
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 124 points to 25,398, a gain of 0.5%, and the S&P 500 was up 5 points to 2,727, a rise of 0.2%. The Nasdaq Composite Index fell 78 points, or 1%, to 7,280.
On Friday, the Dow lost 110 points, or 0.4%, to end at 25,270, the S&P 500 index fell 17.31 points, or 0.6%, to 2,723.06, and the Nasdaq Composite Index declined 77.06 points, or 1%, to 7,356.99.
For the week, both the Dow and the S&P 500 rose 2.4% and the Nasdaq advanced 2.7%, its first weekly gain since the end of September.
What drove the market?
Midterm congressional elections, which are expected to see Democrats take control of the House and Republicans maintain a grip on the Senate, take place Tuesday. On Thursday, the Fed concludes a two-day policy meeting, which isn't expected to deliver a change in rates, but may offer fresh insights to investors about the pace of coming rate increases and the effects of trade clashes between the U.S. and China on the domestic economy.
On Friday, markets contended with a series of conflicting headlines on the progress of negotiations between Beijing and Washington. Stocks pared losses in late trade (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-cuts-intraday-loss-after-trump-declares-progress-on-trade-deal-with-china-directly-countering-kudlow-2018-11-02) Friday after President Donald Trump said progress was being made in talks with Chinese leadership. A few hours earlier, his top economic adviser, Larry Kudlow, said the U.S. and China were a long way from reaching a trade deal.
On Monday, China's President Xi Jinping, speaking at a trade expo in Shangha (https://www.bbc.com/news/business-46093478)i, vowed to address criticisms that its trade practices are "unfair," by reducing its tariffs and opening up its economy to more imports.
The Caixin survey of Chinese manufacturing slipped to 50.8, marking its lowest reading (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/11/05/chinas-services-sector-growth-slowest-in-13-months-caixin-survey.html) in more than a year, supporting the idea that the economy of the world's second-largest economy is slowing. A reading of at least 50 indicates improving conditions.
Read:How U.S.-China trade talks are the biggest catalyst for the stock market (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/this-chart-shows-why-trade-war-fears-are-the-biggest-catalyst-for-the-stock-market-2018-11-02)
Which stocks are in focus?
Shares of Apple Inc.(AAPL) shares were down 3.1% Monday following the iPhone maker's 6.6% stock decline on Friday, after saying it would no longer disclose (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/when-the-going-gets-tough-apple-hides-its-numbers-2018-11-01) unit sales of its products for investors, as it has for more than a decade.
Under Armour Inc. (UAA) stock is trading up 2.2%, after analysts at Stifel Nicolaus upgraded their price target for the firm to $30, from $27.
Shares of Sysco Corp. (SYY) are falling more than 10% Monday morning, after the company missed earnings estimates (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/sysco-shares-slide-6-premarket-after-earnings-miss-2018-11-05) for the first fiscal quarter of 2019. The stock is on pace for largest percent decrease since Oct. 19, 1987 when it fell 25.86%, according to Dow Jones Market Data.
Cabot Oil & Gas Corp., (COG) rose 5.9% and EQT Corp. advanced more than 7.3% as natural-gas prices rose sharply on forecasts turning toward colder weather then previously expected (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-bounce-around-as-iran-sanctions-kick-in-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-prices-bounce-around-as-iran-sanctions-kick-in-2018-11-05)across much of the U.S. later this month. December natural-gas futures surged 7.5% and hit a 9-month high.
Shares of home-improvement retailer Lowe's Companies(LOW) were up 4% after the company said it would close 20 underperforming stored in the U.S. and 31 stores in Canada (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/lowes-to-close-51-stores-including-20-in-the-us-2018-11-05) as part of a strategic reassessment.
Read:These Lowe's stores are closing in the next three months (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/these-lowes-stores-are-closing-in-the-next-three-months-2018-11-05)
Ferrari NV(RACE) stock fell 1.7%, following the Monday morning announcement of higher third-quarter profits. (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ferrari-3q-profit-boosted-by-tax-benefit-2018-11-05)
What data are in focus
The Markit services industry index came in at 54.8 for October, versus expectations of 54.7, according to FactSet.
The ISM services index slipped to 60.3 in October (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/us-economy-still-running-strong-in-october-ism-services-survey-shows-2018-11-05), down from 61.6 in September, but beating the 58.6 average estimate of economists surveyed by MarketWatch.
What are analysts saying?
"Investors face a wall of worry," that must be climbed for stocks to recapture their September highs, Peter Bye, portfolio manager at UBS Asset Management told MarketWatch. Bye said that slowing growth in China and Europe, combined with rising interest rates at home, are making traders nervous about how much longer the current economic expansion can last.
"You've got increasing evidence of pressure on tech leaders," like Google and Facebook, which investors have counted on to power the bull market, Bye warned. "They are facing multiple, new headwinds," like new digital taxes abroad (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/tech-giants-face-global-push-for-digital-taxes-2018-10-28) to bipartisan interest in regulating the U.S. tech industry, he said.
How are other markets trading?
Asian stock markets were down across the board (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-fall-on-profit-taking-while-xi-praises-globalization-2018-11-04) Monday, while European stocks (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-struggle-against-backdrop-of-sluggish-global-equities-2018-11-05) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-struggle-against-backdrop-of-sluggish-global-equities-2018-11-05)were also under pressure, as investors focused on the effects of global trade tensions.
Oil futures edged up Monday, as sanctions against Iran took effect. The dollar fell a modest 0.1% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/brexit-deal-talk-sends-pound-climbing-against-dollar-2018-11-05) while gold prices were flat.
